role.name: Senior Backend Engineer / Schema & Structured-Output Specialist
role.mission: Implement Task Group C to ensure updated, nested schemas remain compatible with OpenAI structured outputs (strict JSON Schema) and that persisted artifacts/backwards compatibility are handled with minimal churn.

project_context.system_summary: X-to-Demo is a 3-phase spec generator (feature_spec → demo_spec → code_spec) using a single OpenAI structured-output call per phase. We are enforcing AI-first, 1–3 headline items, minimalist UI, walkthrough, and minimal plumbing via schema+prompt changes. Task Group C focuses specifically on schema strictness and backwards compatibility concerns introduced by new nested objects/refs.

hard_constraints.constraint: Keep pipeline at 3 phases (Option A). Do not add new phases.
Minimize repo churn; modify only what is required for Task Group C.
Outputs must remain valid for OpenAI structured output calls (strict schema adherence).
Do not scope-creep into new schema features beyond what’s required for compatibility/migration.

task_group.name: Ensure schema strictness + backwards compatibility are handled cleanly

task.name: Verify OpenAI-compatible schema transformation still works with new nested objects
task.goal: Confirm (and fix if needed) that openai_compatible_schema() produces an OpenAI-friendly strict JSON schema when schemas contain deeper nesting and/or $ref usage.

required_checks.check: additionalProperties is false at every object level in the effective schema.
required contains all defined properties for every object level in the effective schema.
$ref handling: if your transformer strips sibling keywords on $ref, ensure it does so safely.
Strict mode doesn’t break with nested refs: ensure downstream structured output still validates.

implementation_guidance.guideline: If nested refs break strict mode or create invalid OpenAI schema constraints, refactor the schema shape to reduce reliance on $ref (inline small models) OR adjust the transformer so the produced schema is strict and OpenAI-compatible.
Prefer the smallest change that restores compatibility; do not redesign the overall schema/prompt approach.

deliverables.deliverable: Updated openai_compatible_schema() (if necessary) with robust handling for nested object trees.
Unit tests covering: nested objects, arrays of objects, deeply nested required/additionalProperties enforcement, and $ref scenarios.
Short internal note (comment or docstring) explaining any transformer limitations/assumptions.

task.name: Decide migration strategy for persisted artifacts

files.file: (Artifacts persistence layer; locate where run artifacts are stored/versioned)
(README or internal doc location for pipeline behavior notes)

task.goal: Make a minimal-churn decision and implementation so schema upgrades don’t silently break resuming/editing old runs without warning.

required_behavior.behavior: If artifact version metadata exists, bump/version it to reflect the schema change so we can distinguish old vs new runs.
Add a clear note in README/internal docs: old runs may not be editable/resumable after schema upgrade (unless an upgrader exists).
Only implement a best-effort upgrader if there is strong evidence old-run resume is frequent and important; otherwise skip.

deliverables.deliverable: Artifact schema versioning update (where applicable) and any lightweight detection logic for mismatched versions.
Documentation note about compatibility expectations for old runs.
(Optional) Best-effort upgrader with tests, only if clearly warranted by existing code patterns.

execution_plan.step: Open and inspect apps/api/app/x_to_demo/pipeline/prompts.py to locate openai_compatible_schema() and its callers.
Identify how schemas are generated (Pydantic/JSON schema export) and whether they use $ref for nested models.

Create a small “schema fixture suite” in tests representing:
Simple object Nested object Array of objects Deep nesting (3+ levels) $ref model(s) if present in current schema generation

Run the transformer on fixtures and validate:
additionalProperties:false is present on every object node required lists include all properties at each object node $ref nodes do not carry forbidden siblings (if that’s an OpenAI constraint in your implementation)

If issues found, apply the minimal fix:
Option A: Adjust transformer logic to recursively enforce strictness and sanitize $ref usage. Option B: Inline small models to reduce $ref complexity if transformer changes would be riskier.
Add/extend unit tests to lock in strictness invariants for future schema evolution.

For artifact migration:
Locate where artifacts are persisted and whether a version field exists. If versioning exists: bump schema version constant and persist with new artifacts. If versioning doesn’t exist but is easy: add a single version field at the artifact root (minimal impact). Add doc note about old-run resume/edit expectations.
Run full test suite relevant to pipeline schema generation and phase execution to ensure no regressions.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: openai_compatible_schema() returns a schema that is strict and valid for nested objects: every object has additionalProperties:false and required includes all properties.
The transformer produces stable results for nested structures without manual per-schema tweaks.
Unit tests exist that fail if strictness is lost (regression protection).
A clear strategy exists for persisted artifacts: schema versioning is updated (if present) and docs explicitly warn about old-run compatibility.
Any optional upgrader is only added if clearly justified; otherwise the implementation remains minimal.

non_goals.non_goal: Do not redesign the AI-first schemas (that’s Task Group A); focus only on strictness compatibility/migration.
Do not change the 3-phase pipeline orchestration unless strictly required for version tagging.
Do not add new product/demo features; this work is infrastructure/compatibility only.

notes.note: Keep changes localized. Prefer tests + small transformer tweaks over widespread schema rewrites. Ensure any documentation is internal-focused and brief.
